iconicAnchor.label: Sequential comic page grammar
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: A complete comic page establishes panels, gutters, balloons, captions, sound effects, recurring characters, and changes in shot scale as a system for controlling sequence.

sources.title: Collections Policy Statement: Comic Books and Related Materials
supports: Comics are sequential narrative artifacts whose meaning depends on the relationship among images, text, recurring figures, publication formats, and reading order.

sources.title: Comics and Comic Characters classification guidance
supports: The institutional guidance distinguishes comics, strips, books, characters, and related formats, reinforcing that one isolated pop illustration is not a comic sequence.

bundledReferenceRationale: The four-panel rainy-city sequence is an excellent lead. Gutters, repeated character/location, action continuity, speech balloons, and the recovered-map payoff establish true sequential storytelling at both scales. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/comic-panel/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
